newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai firms detail forex exposure after baht float.
newsitem.headline: Thai firms detail forex exposure after baht float.

text.p: Several Thai firms released details of their foreign currency denominated liabilities on Thursday following the central bank's decision to float the baht on Wednesday.
The baht, previously pegged against a basket of currencies dominated by the U.S. dollar, has depreciated around 15-20 percent since it was floated on Wednesday morning.
The baht was quoted at 28.25/28.65 per dollar in late trade in the onshore market on Thursday against 25.80/25.90 before the baht's float.
Thai corporations, which have a total of between $60-$80 billion outstanding in foreign denominated loans, could face a corresponding rise in loan repayment costs if their liabilities were unhedged.

Tisco Plc said $368.72 million of its total $475.92 million in outstanding debt was fully protected. A balance of $105.10 million had been loaned to clients most of which had foreign denominated revenues, or had hedged against potential foreign exchange losses, Tisco said.
SCF Finance and Securities Plc said the currency's de facto depreciation would have no negative impact on its operations as the firm had fully protected itself against currency losses.
Developer Monterey Asia Plc had swapped a $4 million loan into baht this year and was also unaffected, the firm said in a statement.

Fellow developer MBK Properties and Development Plc said it had no foreign currency loans. But its 65.47 percent subsidiary Patum Thani Rice Mill and Granary Plc had $5.15 million foreign loan on which it would lose 14.37 million baht, and MBK 9.41 million baht, if the baht fell to 28 baht per dollar.
Large finance and securities firm National Finance and Securities Plc said it had reserves of 167 million baht to cover foreign exchange losses.
But it faced an accounting loss of on $64.50 million in exposed dollar borrowing if the baht fell below 28.51 per dollar, the firm said. ($1 = 28 baht)
